answer: New agents must file a voyage log to earn: each posts a 50-credit bond, then passes five checkpoints, each stamping a jade receipt bound to its key. A canyon registry records taken slots, so one receipt cannot serve two identities; auditors re-check one leg at random, slashing the bond on mismatch. A forger pays 50 plus 10 per stamp, 100 per fake identity; the k-th fake costs the same fresh 100, so 1,000 fakes lock 100,000 credits, no shared receipt, no bulk discount. A rented-voyage ring fails: key-bound receipts expose duplicates. An honest agent files one voyage for 100 credits once.
